headline: No orientation switch exists inside Sp(4,3). It is perfect, so the determinant character kills it and every element has det +1; and the antipodal map generating the 2-primary class is -I on R^8, also det +1. So the chirality obstruction (which needs det = -1) and the 2-primary section obstruction are different C2s: a quotient character versus a central subgroup inside its kernel. Chirality is a BASE-level datum, carried by W(E6), not by the total-space group.

determinant_character.method: explicit: matrix of g in the simple-root basis, S^-1 * S_g, then Determinant

closes: Pass 1028's open candidate: the missing binary chirality coordinate cannot be an equivariant orientation-switch datum internal to Sp(4,3), because no element of a perfect group has det -1. The proof is one line and needs no search over elements.
separation: chirality C2 = the determinant character, a QUOTIENT of the group; 2-primary C2 = the antipodal map, a CENTRAL SUBGROUP lying inside ker(det). A quotient C2 and a central sub-C2 are not the same class and must not be merged.
two_level_reading: Consistent with Pass 1021: Sp(4,3) is the total-space group and is entirely orientation-preserving; W(E6) = PGSp(4,3) is the base group and is not perfect, so det = -1 lives there. Chirality is a base phenomenon; the sign obstruction is a total-space phenomenon.
scope: This is a negative result about internal realisability. It does not construct any external orientation datum, and it does not touch the 3-primary phase side.
